lines.trans: Good morning, Clara! Good morning, sir! What a bright morning after the rain.
Good morning, Javier! Did you sleep well under the wooden beams?
The best sleep all month, and the shower water came out nice and hot!
Hot! Do you hear that, Clara? Modern, reliable, five-star hot water!
Old brick buildings usually take ages to warm up the top floor.
Please write that down! Hot water on the third floor: ten out of ten!
Excuse me? Ten out of ten?
What Ernesto means is... we hope every guest feels ten out of ten here!

lines.trans: No, Clara, let us be honest professionals! Sir, we deeply respect the Valencia travel guide!
The Valencia travel guide? Wait a moment: do you think I am a hotel inspector?

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: Last night your notebook lay open on the counter and we saw nine out of ten...
Aha! Come out to the courtyard with me for a minute: I will show you what I really do!
See you soon!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle abierto.

examples.text: Abro la ventana por la mañana.
examples.trans: I open the window in the morning.
Yesterday we opened the shop early.

meanings.note: Feminine noun that takes el in the singular before stressed initial /a/ (el agua fría).

examples.text: Quiero un vaso de agua fría.
examples.trans: I want a glass of cold water.

examples.text: El agua de la ducha sale caliente.
examples.trans: The shower water comes out hot.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization or understanding.

examples.trans: Ah, now I understand the map!
Oh really? What good news.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Single word meaning 'last night' (never la última noche).

examples.text: Anoche llovió mucho en la ciudad.
examples.trans: Last night it rained heavily in the city.
Did you sleep well last night?

meanings.note: Placed after a noun, means 'historic' or 'old-fashioned'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.

examples.text: Encantada, Tomás, ¡siempre que nadie hable de vender pianos antiguos!
examples.trans: Gladly, Tomas, as long as nobody talks about selling old pianos!

meanings.note: Usually plural (los apuntes) for written notes.

examples.trans: The note is here.

examples.text: Vemos los apuntes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notes from the door.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

bajar.gloss: to go down; to bring down; to lower

meanings.en: to go down; to bring down; to lower
meanings.note: Works both intransitively (go downstairs) and transitively (bring down).

examples.text: Bajo a la cocina a preparar té.
examples.trans: I go down to the kitchen to make tea.

examples.text: Bajamos las maletas por la escalera.
examples.trans: We bring the suitcases down the stairs.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (bien caliente), means 'nice and hot'.

examples.trans: Everything is going very well today.
The tea comes out nice and hot.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Invariable before masculine or feminine singular nouns (cada día, cada mañana).

examples.trans: I open the cafe every morning.
Each room has its own key.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: calienta).

examples.text: Caliento la leche en un cazo.
examples.trans: I warm the milk in a saucepan.

examples.text: El sol de la mañana calienta el patio.
examples.trans: The morning sun warms the courtyard.

meanings.note: Describes hot drinks, food, or water.

examples.trans: It is a hot piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene, señora: té caliente de menta con miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea with honey.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Faltan cinco minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is five minutes to twelve.

examples.text: Tenemos cinco mesas en el patio.
examples.trans: We have five tables in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Can take el or la, alongside dedicated feminine clienta.

examples.trans: The guest is here.

examples.text: Vemos los clientes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the guests from the door.

meanings.note: Special fused form of con + mí.

examples.text: Ven conmigo al patio un minuto.
examples.trans: Come out to the courtyard with me for a minute.
Do you want to have breakfast with me?

meanings.note: Preterite 3rd sg/pl spells y: creyó, creyeron.

examples.text: Creo que el tren llega a tiempo.
examples.trans: I think the train is arriving on time.

examples.text: No podía creer tanta buena suerte.
examples.trans: He could not believe such good luck.

meanings.note: Bound paper notebook.

examples.trans: The notebook is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cuadernos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notebooks from the door.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?
Tell me the truth without fear.

dedicar.gloss: to dedicate; to do for a living (dedicarse a)

meanings.en: to dedicate; to do for a living (dedicarse a)
meanings.note: ¿A qué te dedicas? / ¿A qué se dedica? asks someone's profession.

examples.trans: What do you do for a living right now?

examples.text: Dedica la tarde a tocar el piano.
examples.trans: She devotes the afternoon to playing the piano.

meanings.note: Después de + noun/infinitive means 'after'.

examples.trans: We will talk after breakfast.
What do we do after that?

meanings.note: Diez sobre diez = ten out of ten.

examples.trans: There are ten minutes left before starting.
Your front desk deserves a ten.

meanings.note: Disculpe (usted) / Disculpa (tú) is polite 'excuse me'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, do you know what time it is?

examples.text: Nos disculpamos por el pequeño retraso.
examples.trans: We apologized for the brief delay.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue in present: duermo; o -> u in preterite 3rd: durmió).

examples.trans: I sleep eight hours every night.
Last night I slept wonderfully here.

meanings.note: Darse una ducha = to take a shower.

examples.trans: The shower is here.

examples.text: Vemos las duchas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the showers from the door.

meanings.note: Masculine despite ending in -a: el día, ¡Buenos días!.

examples.trans: The day is here.

examples.text: Vemos los días desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the days from the door.

meanings.note: Multi-storey town building.

examples.trans: The building is here.

examples.text: Vemos los edificios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the buildings from the door.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Means both 'to show something' and 'to teach'.

examples.text: Te enseño el patio de la casa.
examples.trans: I will show you the house courtyard.

examples.text: La profesora enseñó piano durante muchos años.
examples.trans: La profesora taught piano for many years.

meanings.note: Neuter pronoun; por eso = that is why.

examples.trans: That is why I brought two umbrellas.
What does that mean exactly?

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.
We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: De cinco estrellas = five-star.

examples.trans: The star is here.

examples.text: Vemos las estrellas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stars from the door.

meanings.note: Por favor literally means 'as a favour'.

examples.trans: The favour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los favores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the favours from the door.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.trans: It is a reliable piece.

examples.text: ¡Caliente! ¿Oye eso, Clara? ¡Agua caliente moderna, fiable y de cinco estrellas!
examples.trans: Hot! Do you hear that, Clara? Modern, reliable, five-star hot water!

meanings.note: La guía de viajes = the travel guidebook.

examples.trans: The guidebook is here.

examples.text: Vemos las guías desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the guidebooks from the door.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Plural los hoteles.

examples.trans: The hotel is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hoteles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hotels from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine: la inspectora.

examples.trans: The inspector is here.

examples.text: Vemos los inspectores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the inspectors from the door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: De ladrillo = made of brick.

examples.trans: The brick is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ladrillos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bricks from the door.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.trans: The windows face the garden.
We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Plural indirect object pronoun.

examples.trans: I will prepare breakfast for you all right away.
I owe you both the whole truth.

meanings.note: Bajo la lluvia = in the rain.

examples.text: La lluvia es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The rain is very important here.
We talk about the rain.

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)
meanings.note: Direct object pronoun before verbs (lo veo), and neuter article in lo que ('what') or lo mejor ('the best').

examples.text: Ya lo veo encima del estante.
examples.trans: I see it now on the shelf.

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Describes a sunny morning or airy room.

examples.trans: It is a bright piece.
What a bright morning

meanings.note: De madera = wooden.

examples.trans: The wood is here.

examples.text: Vemos las maderas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the woods from the door.

meanings.note: La mañana = the morning; mañana (without article) = tomorrow.

examples.text: Por la mañana servimos café caliente.
examples.trans: In the morning we serve hot coffee.
See you tomorrow at eight!

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?
I live here and I work here.

meanings.note: Irregular comparative/superlative of bueno; plural mejores.

examples.text: Esta ventana tiene la mejor vista.
examples.trans: This window has the best view.
Today the radiator heats better.

meanings.note: Plural los meses.

examples.trans: The month is here.

examples.text: Vemos los meses desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the months from the door.

meanings.note: En cinco minutos = in five minutes.

examples.trans: The minute is here.

examples.text: Vemos los minutos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the minutes from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of antiguo.

examples.trans: It is a modern piece.

examples.text: ¡Caliente! ¿Oye eso, Clara? ¡Agua caliente moderna, fiable y de cinco estrellas!
examples.trans: Hot! Do you hear that, Clara? Modern, reliable, five-star hot water!

meanings.note: De momento = for now.

examples.trans: The moment is here.

examples.text: Vemos los momentos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the moments from the door.

meanings.note: Reception desk or shop counter.

examples.trans: The counter is here.

examples.text: Vemos los mostradores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the counters from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees before nouns (mucha agua, muchos años); invariable after verbs (llueve mucho).

examples.trans: Today we have a lot of work.
Thank you very much for the coffee.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: Las nueve = nine o'clock.

examples.text: El tren llega a las nueve en punto.
examples.trans: The train arrives at nine on the dot.
We saw a nine out of ten.

meanings.note: Irregular: oigo, oyes, oye, oímos, oís, oyen; ¡Oiga! / ¡Oye! gets someone's attention.

examples.trans: Can you hear me clearly on the phone?

examples.text: Acabo de oír pasos en la escalera.
examples.trans: I just heard footsteps on the stairs.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: Planta baja = ground floor; primera planta = first floor; also a green plant.

examples.trans: The floor / storey is here.

examples.text: Vemos las plantas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the floor / storeys from the door.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine/feminine and as an adjective (plural profesionales).

examples.trans: The professional is here.

examples.text: Vemos los profesionales desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the professionals from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon!

examples.trans: See you soon and safe travels!

examples.text: Esta mañana me desperté muy pronto.
examples.trans: This morning I woke up very early.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

quedar.gloss: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)

meanings.en: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)
meanings.note: Versatile verb: quedan dos ('two left'), le queda bien ('suits you'), quedar al mediodía ('meet at noon'), quedarse ('stay').

examples.trans: Only two vacant rooms are left.

examples.text: Esa chaqueta te queda muy bien.
examples.trans: That jacket suits you very well.

meanings.note: Sin querer = by accident; querer decir = to mean.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or hot tea?
I opened it by accident.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Respetamos el descanso de los vecinos.
examples.trans: We respect the neighbours' rest.

examples.text: Todos respetan las normas del patio.
examples.trans: Everyone respects the courtyard rules.

salir.gloss: to go out; to come out; to leave

meanings.en: to go out; to come out; to leave
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg salgo; salir corriendo = run out.

examples.text: El pan acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The bread just came out of the oven.
I leave early for the station.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

sentir.gloss: to feel; to be sorry (lo siento)

meanings.en: to feel; to be sorry (lo siento)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie in present, e -> i in preterite 3rd: sintió).

examples.text: Lo siento mucho por la espera.
examples.trans: I am very sorry about the wait.

examples.text: Aquí cada huésped se siente en casa.
examples.trans: Here every guest feels at home.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Takes el when talking about someone (el señor Martín), no article when addressing directly (¡Buenos días, señor!).

examples.trans: The sir is here.

examples.text: Vemos los señores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sirs from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number.

examples.trans: It is a honest piece.

examples.text: Señor, antes de subir, le debo una disculpa sincera.
examples.trans: Sir, before going upstairs, I owe you an honest apology.

sobre.gloss: on; upon; about; out of (nueve sobre diez)

meanings.en: on; upon; about; out of (nueve sobre diez)
meanings.note: Sobre todo = above all / mostly; also a homograph noun el sobre ('envelope').

examples.text: Deja la llave sobre el mostrador.
examples.trans: Leave the key on the counter.

examples.text: Sacó nueve sobre diez en la prueba.
examples.trans: She scored nine out of ten on the test.

soler.gloss: to usually do; to tend to (soler + infinitive)

meanings.en: to usually do; to tend to (soler + infinitive)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: suelo, suele, suelen) used in present/imperfect + infinitive.

examples.text: Suelo tomar café a las ocho.
examples.trans: I usually have coffee at eight.

examples.text: Estos muros suelen guardar el fresco.
examples.trans: These walls usually keep the air cool.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: sueño).

examples.text: Anoche soñé con un viaje en tren.
examples.trans: Last night I dreamed about a train journey.

examples.text: Siempre sueña con tener su propia cafetería.
examples.trans: She always dreams of having her own cafe.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Shortened form of tanto used before adjectives and adverbs (¡qué mañana tan luminosa!).

examples.trans: What a peaceful courtyard!

examples.text: ¿Por qué sale el agua tan fría?
examples.trans: Why is the water running so cold?

meanings.note: Tardar diez minutos en llegar = take ten minutes to get there.

examples.text: Tardo cinco minutos en llegar al puente.
examples.trans: It takes me five minutes to reach the bridge.

examples.text: El agua caliente no tardó nada en subir.
examples.trans: The hot water took no time at all to reach upstairs.

meanings.note: Shortens to tercer before masculine singular nouns (el tercer escalón).

examples.trans: It is a third piece.
Come on, race you to the third floor!

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.
See you later in the courtyard!

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.trans: The truth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verdades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the truths from the door.

meanings.note: Guía de viajes = travel guide.

examples.trans: The trip is here.

examples.text: Vemos los viajes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the trips from the door.

meanings.note: Vigas de madera = wooden roof beams.

examples.trans: The ceiling beam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las vigas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ceiling beams from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Carries a written accent on ú.

examples.trans: It is a last piece.

examples.text: Diez, once, doce. Exacto hasta la última moneda. ¡Gracias!
examples.trans: Ten, eleven, twelve. Exact to the last coin. Thank you!
